rule_context.boundary: Architecture is defined independently of defects. Do not materialize a broken starter from this packet before A3 topology approval.

candidates.name: generic_ansible_playbook_resource
candidates.reason: An execution-event abstraction gives weak Read and drift semantics and encourages replay-oriented behavior.

candidates.name: ansible_backed_managed_os_resources
candidates.reason: A bounded managed-object provider gives real CRUD, drift reconciliation, stable identity, failure-state, idempotency, and Terraform state-lifecycle behavior.

candidates.name: provider_defined_terraform_state_store
candidates.reason: Provider-defined state storage is a separate concern and would distract from managed-resource lifecycle correctness.

candidates.name: remote_multi_host_ansible_orchestrator
candidates.reason: SSH, bastions, Vault, Galaxy, dynamic inventory, and fleet orchestration make transport integration the dominant difficulty and reduce determinism.

product_contract.terraform_state_contract: Terraform Core owns the physical state. Resource methods publish state only through Terraform Plugin Framework response-state APIs.
product_contract.ownership_rule: One Terraform resource owns one external object key. Overlapping ownership of the same path, user, group, or cron name is outside the supported contract.
forbidden_semantic_substitutes: terraform_data used as an execution wrapper

dependencies.compatibility_note: Use the Go 1.24-compatible Plugin Framework line to remain compatible with the repository's current canonical Go runtime.

runtime_flow: Terraform Core starts terraform-provider-ansibleops through the provider plugin protocol.
Provider registration exposes exactly ten ansibleops managed resources.
Create, Update, and Delete translate desired resource state into typed internal specifications.
Typed specifications are rendered as ephemeral Ansible tasks or playbooks.
The common runner invokes ansible-playbook using argv isolation and context-aware process control.
Successful mutations publish Terraform state; failed mutations return diagnostics without claiming an uncommitted transition.
Read uses native Linux observers to inspect actual target state and never invokes Ansible.
Observed state is normalized and written back to Terraform so normal plan and refresh can detect drift.

terraform_core: physical Terraform state in verifier workspaces
prior state, proposed state, refresh state, dependency graph

resource_contracts.name: ansibleops_file
resource_contracts.create_update: Ensure a regular file exists with requested managed metadata without repeated timestamp mutation.
resource_contracts.read: Inspect path existence, object type, mode, owner, and group.
resource_contracts.delete: Ensure the managed path is absent.

resource_contracts.name: ansibleops_directory
resource_contracts.create_update: Ensure a directory exists with requested managed metadata.
resource_contracts.read: Inspect path type, mode, owner, and group.
resource_contracts.delete: Ensure the managed directory path is absent.

resource_contracts.name: ansibleops_copy
resource_contracts.create_update: Copy source content to destination; source_digest makes source-content changes explicit to Terraform planning.
resource_contracts.read: Observe destination type, metadata, and SHA-256 content digest.

resource_contracts.name: ansibleops_template
resource_contracts.create_update: Render source template using deterministic variables and install destination.
resource_contracts.read: Observe destination type, metadata, and rendered content digest.
resource_contracts.normalization: vars is semantically unordered and must be canonicalized deterministically.

resource_contracts.name: ansibleops_line
resource_contracts.create_update: Manage one named line contract without duplicate insertion.
resource_contracts.read: Inspect the file and report whether the managed line contract is satisfied.
resource_contracts.delete: Remove only the managed line matching the resource contract.

resource_contracts.name: ansibleops_block
resource_contracts.read: Parse marker boundaries and compare the current managed block.
resource_contracts.delete: Remove only the named managed block.

resource_contracts.name: ansibleops_symlink
resource_contracts.create_update: Ensure symlink path points to requested target.
resource_contracts.read: Use lstat and readlink; distinguish missing, symlink, and wrong object type.
resource_contracts.delete: Remove the link path without deleting the link target.

resource_contracts.name: ansibleops_user
resource_contracts.create_update: Ensure local user attributes and supplementary groups match requested managed values.
resource_contracts.read: Observe passwd and group databases using native OS APIs or commands.
resource_contracts.delete: Ensure user is absent; home removal follows remove_home_on_destroy only.

resource_contracts.name: ansibleops_group
resource_contracts.create_update: Ensure local group exists with requested managed gid.

resource_contracts.name: ansibleops_cron
resource_contracts.create_update: Manage one named crontab entry through Ansible.
resource_contracts.read: Inspect the user's crontab and parse the named managed entry without requiring a running cron daemon.
resource_contracts.delete: Remove only the named managed entry.

cross_resource_invariants: All ten resource types are registered as real Terraform managed resources.
Stable identity derives only from the external object key, never from mutable desired values.
Read is side-effect free and never invokes ansible-playbook.
Create and Update publish new Terraform state only after successful Ansible completion.
Failed Update preserves the last successfully applied state.
Delete completes only after successful teardown or verified already-absent state.
Clean plan and refresh do not execute Ansible.
Ansible commands execute without shell interpolation.
Paths containing spaces and shell metacharacters are passed as literal arguments or data.
Context cancellation, timeout, and non-zero Ansible exit are failures.
Generated playbooks are cleaned up on success, failure, timeout, and cancellation.
Observed modes, ownership, identifiers, and schedule values use stable canonical representations.
Diagnostics are bounded and full command output is not persisted in Terraform state.
production_characteristics: Ten differentiated Terraform resource contracts sharing four backend families.
Real Terraform provider server entrypoint and Plugin Framework lifecycle integration.
Separate mutation and observation paths so refresh cannot replay configuration management.
Persistent external reality in the Linux filesystem, passwd/group databases, and crontab.
Restart-safe behavior because durable Terraform state is owned by Terraform Core rather than process memory.
Shared validation, normalization, diagnostics, task generation, execution, timeout, and cleanup layers.
Representative examples and solver-visible product and lifecycle documentation.

strict_scale.scale_rationale: Scale comes from ten real schemas and observers plus shared lifecycle, execution, normalization, validation, and diagnostics. Boilerplate duplication, generated code, vendored dependencies, dead modules, and prompt-extension padding do not count.
strict_scale.f2p_behavioral_test_target: 25-30 non-duplicative tests arising from shared lifecycle invariants and representative resource semantics

excluded_scope: SSH bastions and remote fleet orchestration
provider-defined Terraform state stores or backends

next_gate.requirement: Define 4-8 root-cause clusters and 20-30 causally related observable manifestations against this clean architecture. Do not materialize the broken starter before independent approval of that topology.
